caption: A Money Model Happened. Offer #1 + Offer #2 + Offer #3 = money. A Money Model is a sequence of offers, not one offer.
MONEY MODEL. The four offer types in order: 1 Attraction, 2 Upsells, 3 Downsells, 4 Continuity. The spine of the whole book.
The Free vs Discount Continuum (100% off to 0% off, highest demand to lowest) plus the Attraction magnet icon. Free and discount are the same lever at different settings.
Win Your Money Back. Before: pay, get the thing. After: do X, in Y time, within Z rules, and get your money back.
Giveaways, the three steps: 1 give away one free amazing thing to get lots of leads, 2 select the grand prize winner, 3 offer everyone else the product at a discount (second place prize winners).
Decoy Offer. The lead is shown (A) the free or cheap lower-value offer, or (B) the stacked premium offer at amazing value. Most take B.
Decoy Offer, the same play drawn with a percentage-off decoy instead of a free one.
Buy X Get Y Free. Products: buy 1 shirt at $20, get 2 free. Services: buy X months, get Y months free. Plus the Boot Factory sign - Buy 1 Pair Get Two Pair Free.
Buy 3 shirts for $30 versus buy 1 shirt for $30 and get 2 free. Same money, very different offer.
Buy 3 shirts for $20 ($6.67 each, a 33% discount) versus buy 1 shirt for $20 and get 2 free. Free beats discount at the same price.
Buy X Get Y Free variants. More free stuff beats less free stuff, and the free things do not have to be the same as the paid things.
More cheap free things can beat fewer expensive ones. Buy 1 shirt get 1 free versus buy 1 shirt get 3 socks free.
Pay Less Now or Pay More Later. (A) free now, then $297 after, or (B) $97 now plus three bonuses free, today only.
Free Goodwill Offer. Ask the reader to help someone they will never meet by leaving a review.
The Burger, Fries and Soda Method. Old way: sell the $2 burger at $0.25 profit. New way: add drink and supersize for 8x then 11.6x gross profit per sale.
The Classic Upsell. Problem to Upsell to Solution. 'You don't want anything besides X and Y do you?' - 'No, that's fine.'
The 'Magnetic' Middle. Pricing small, medium and large so the option you want becomes the obvious one.
Menu Upsell, the four tactics: 1 unsell what they don't need, 2 prescribe what they do need, 3 ask if they prefer A or B, 4 make it easy to pay (card on file).
The 'Economist' Play. With only two options people take the cheap one. Add a decoy third at the same price as A+B and more people take the bundle.
Anchor Upsell. Present the $1,000 thing, get the gasp, come to the rescue with the $100 thing. Relief closes the sale.
Rollover Upsell. Credit what they already paid toward the next offer - 'let's credit what you already won toward this one.'
The Gift Card Play. Sell $200 gift cards for $20, cap at two per person, they cannot be used on yourself - so they get given away and roll over into an offer.
Payment Plan Downsells. Layaway and financing, half now half later, 3-pay, evenly spread payments.
Trial With Penalty. Free service as long as you show up, do the homework and leave a review - or you pay.
How I Sell Free Trials, steps 1 and 2: use the free trial as a downsell (after the big and small package), and always get a credit card.
How I Sell Free Trials, step 3: set the expectation of staying and paying before the trial starts.
How I Sell Free Trials, steps 4 and 5: explain how the fees motivate them, and make sales meetings part of the trial.
Feature Downsells. Take features off the original offer, lower the price, and ask 'how about now?'
Downsell Offers Conclusion. The down arrow - everybody buys something.
Continuity Bonus Offers. (A) pay $600, or (B) get the $600 thing free by joining at $200/mo.
One-time price versus continuity. The graph of how much bigger the standalone price has to be to push a given percentage of buyers into continuity: 1.33x for 50%, 2.66x for 90%.
Continuity Discount Offers. Free duration plus contract commitment - 3 months free for a 12-month commitment.
The four ways to apply a continuity discount, 1 and 2: up front, and at the end.
The four ways to apply a continuity discount, 3 and 4: spread over time (they keep the discount), and after the first 1-2 payments.
Waived Fee Offer. (A) $5,000 one-time fee plus $1,000/mo month-to-month, or (B) the fee waived with a 12-month contract.
Continuity Offers Conclusion. The continuity circle - the only thing better than getting someone to buy once is getting them to buy again.
Make Your Own Money Model. The four icons in sequence: Attraction, Upsell, Downsell, Continuity. Start with one, add the next only when the first is reliable.
Ten Years In Ten Minutes. The treasure map - the whole book condensed.
